items.headline: Scandal-hit Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaking giant into turmoil
items.blurb: US lawmakers now want to question him over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy.
items.text: Jensen Huang has abruptly quit as chief executive of AI chipmaking giant Nvidia after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves from Silicon Valley to Capitol Hill. Nvidia is now under scrutiny from US lawmakers in Washington DC demanding Huang answer questions over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy. One of the world's most valuable companies as a result of the AI boom, Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress, called an emergency meeting of her executive team to discuss the company's future. His alleged conduct not only potentially crossed professional boundaries, but has made Nvidia the target of questions from US politicians who have expressed concern about national security risks. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. items.blurb: After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’ The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded…
items.text: After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’ The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation. Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter , which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October. Five days later, the Atlantic published an article titled “Yet another literary prize winner seems to be AI”, in which the author and journalist Vauhini Vara said the AI-detection software Pangram, which itself uses AI, had deemed the story to be almost completely artificially generated. The Caine prize chair, Ellah Wakatama, said in a statement : “From our detailed investigation, we feel the evidence is clear: The Blue Fighter was human-written. items.headline: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
items.blurb: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.
items.text: Ukraine's president has welcomed a pledge from US envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, to include delegates from the European Union in the next round of peace talks with Russia. European leaders have expressed deepening security concerns this week, and Volodymyr Zelensky said bringing them into the talks would ensure the EU has a "voice" in negotiations. Kushner and Witkoff met Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday evening as part of a busy day of shuttle diplomacy - they met Vladimir Putin in Moscow earlier, who said that Russia's position on the war - and its demand for territory - has not changed. The meetings follow talks in Abu Dhabi last week that failed to reach a breakthrough in ending the war. But Thursday did see Russia and Ukraine agree to another prisoner exchange - the largest swap yet since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. Kushner said it would return "thousands of people to their families", but further details like how many prisoners would be exchanged or a timeline, were not given. items.headline: Spanish court suspends far-right group over alleged hate crimes
items.blurb: Judge orders office shut and accounts blocked after 14 arrests and the seizure of more than 20 firearms.
items.text: A Spanish judge has suspended the activities of the ultra-right group Nucleo Nacional as part of an investigation into alleged hate crimes and illegal association. The court in the northern city of Gijon announced the ruling on Thursday, ordering the group’s office shut and its social media content and bank accounts blocked. The move follows the arrest last week of 14 of its members on suspicion of inciting hatred against vulnerable groups and people with opposing ideologies. The decision comes ahead of Spain’s general election on November 29 and a day after the first nationwide general strike in 14 years. In a video posted on X, an unnamed Nucleo Nacional representative wearing a black shirt with the group’s logo said the movement was a victim of “persecution and political repression”. Nucleo Nacional describes itself as a political movement. On its website, which has now been blocked and suspended by court order, it says it seeks a “national awakening”. The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire. “I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine . I think there’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping we get to at some stage,” Hamilton said in October. A ceasefire agreement reached last year has halted major combat operations in Gaza, but the amount of aid reaching the territory continues to fall far short of the agreed-upon minimum of 600 trucks a day. items.headline: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
items.blurb: More than 900 victims are thought to have fallen prey to the FaceStealer scheme in the last 18 months.
items.text: State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say. More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau. "The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman. This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from the company. US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim. Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software. items.headline: Chris Van Hollen to run for US Senate majority leader
items.blurb: Van Hollen's entry into the race follows Democratic sweeps in elections and challenges veteran leader Schumer.
items.text: US Senator Chris Van Hollen has said he is running for Senate Majority Leader as the Democrats gear up to take charge of the US Congress in January following a Democratic landslide in midterm elections on November 3. Van Hollen said in a post on X, late on Thursday: “In this election, Americans called on us to unrig an economy rigged against working people & fueled by political corruption”, “To deliver, we need new leadership”, he said, adding that “This isn’t about any one person – it’s about answering that call” Calls were mounting on Van Hollen to throw his hat in the race for the senate majority leader amid some opposition to minority leader Senator Chuck Schumer’s continued tenure after he faced criticism over how he has handled the Democratic Caucus during the Trump presidency.

items.headline: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
items.blurb: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
items.text: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said. The health ministry gave the casualty toll, adding more than 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment. Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways. items.blurb: The attack is thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an open stretch of the Baltic Sea.
items.text: Finnish officials have confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, although little is known about the strike. Ukraine's SBU security service said it targeted the ship Naro-Fominsk as part of a broader drone operation against Russia's Ust-Luga oil export depot on the Baltic coast. The attack, thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an area of the Baltic Sea open to civilian maritime traffic, has raised questions about whether Ukraine could expand its strikes. Helsinki has been one of Kyiv's closest European allies, and Finnish officials have described the incident as a direct result of Russia's continued full-scale war. Finland's military has given few details of the incident, but it appears to have taken place in a narrow stretch some distance from the Finnish coast. The country's Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen was adamant that the situation in the Baltic Sea remained stable and safe and that there was no threat of any kind to marine traffic. items.headline: Kolkata-Sairang train derailment: Preliminary probe points to faulty braking system
items.blurb: A six-member probe team, in its report, found that the system primarily responsible for applying brakes in the coaches, technically known as the BP angle cock, was in an isolated condition in the locomotive
items.text: Officials and rescuers inspect the derailed coaches of a passenger train near Guwahati, on November 11, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP A preliminary probe into the derailment of the Kolkata-Sairang Express at Digaru Railway Station in Assam on November 11 has pointed to a malfunctioning main braking system on the train. A six-member probe team, in its report, found that the system primarily responsible for applying brakes in the coaches, technically known as the BP angle cock, was in an isolated condition in the locomotive. "This may be the reason for this accident, as the brakes may not have been applied when the FP/BP angle cock of the loco was in an isolated condition," a joint note prepared by the probe team on the day of the accident said. It further stated that the train crew applied the brakes, "but the brakes may not have been applied as the angle cock was previously in the closed position". items.blurb: As HT reported earlier, Delhi’s air quality deteriorated sharply on Thursday, with the city’s PM2.5 concentration more than doubling in 24 hours.
items.text: Delhi’s air quality deteriorated into the “severe” zone — the worst grade on the government’s pollution scale— on Friday morning, with a thick, smoky haze continuing to envelop the Capital. According to HT’s real-time air quality dashboar d and the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 403 at 7.30am, 82 points higher than the previous 24 hours. Delhi last recorded severe air quality on January 19, when the AQI stood at 410. CPCB classifies an AQI of 0–50 as “good”, 51–100 as “satisfactory”, 101–200 as “moderate”, 201–300 as “poor”, 301–400 as “very poor” and 401–500 as “severe”. HT reported earlier that Delhi’s air quality deteriorated sharply on Thursday, with the city’s PM2.5 concentration more than doubling in 24 hours to 244 micrograms per cubic metre by 6pm — four times the national standard. items.blurb: The meeting comes amid tensions between China and the Philippines, and is expected to cover economic security, critical technologies and maritime awareness.
items.text: Quad member states are expected to unveil several deliverables, mainly focused on economic security and strategic infrastructure, at the leaders’ summit expected to be held on the margins of the Asean Summit in Manila next week, people familiar with the matter said. The upcoming Quad Leaders’ Summit — the first gathering of the leaders of India, Australia, Japan and the US since September 2024 — is set to be hosted by the US, the people said on condition of anonymity. India was set to chair the leaders’ summit in 2025, but its efforts to arrange the meeting last year were stymied by lack of clarity on US President Donald Trump ’s travel plans. The deliverables expected to be unveiled at the upcoming summit were finalised at the Quad foreign ministers’ meeting on the margins of the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta on October 31, the people said. The foreign ministers’ meet resulted in several outcomes, including the provision of technical and financial aid worth more than $85 million to back access to trusted artificial intelligence across the Indo-Pacific. items.headline: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
items.blurb: In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%
items.text: India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment and faster creation of high-quality jobs to achieve the medium-term potential growth of 6.8%, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday (November 12, 2026). In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%. The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in Washington. “But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI . The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs. Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India. Last month, the IMF raised India’s growth forecast for fiscal year 2027

items.headline: National Tribal Literary Festival begins in Delhi; focus on preserving oral traditions
items.blurb: Union tribal affairs minister Jual Oram stressed the need for systematic documentation of tribal literature, folk songs, folktales and oral traditions
items.text: The second edition of the National Tribal Literary Festival 2026 began on Thursday in Delhi, bringing together tribal writers, poets, researchers and language experts from across the country to deliberate on preserving indigenous languages, oral traditions and literary heritage. Organised by the Union ministry of tribal affairs at the India Habitat Centre as part of the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas Pakhwada, the two-day festival is themed “From Oral Tradition to Contemporary Tribal Literature”. Inaugurating the festival, Union tribal affairs minister Jual Oram stressed the need for systematic documentation of tribal literature, folk songs, folktales and oral traditions, saying the effort must involve not only writers but also lyricists, musicians, folk artists and digital content creators. “Preserving tribal languages and oral traditions is central to building Viksit Bharat 2047,” the minister said. Pointing out that several tribal languages do not have a written script and some dialects are on the verge of extinction, Oram said the absence of a script should not become an obstacle to their preservation. For the first half of FY27, NHC Foods posted total income of ₹821.45 crore, an increase of 282 per cent from ₹214.68 crore a year earlier. Profit rose nearly 13-fold to ₹38.68 crore, compared with ₹3.01 crore in the year-ago period. Commenting on the performance, Managing Director Satyam Joshi said, "We are encouraged by the strong performance this quarter and in the first half and remain focused on sustaining this growth momentum. Our strategy is centred on expanding our operations, strengthening our presence in the agri commodities and food processing sectors, and pursuing opportunities that complement our capabilities. items.headline: Elon Musk's SpaceX-Tesla mega merger could be announced in December: What could derail the deal?
items.blurb: SpaceX and Tesla are advancing merger talks, with an announcement potentially coming as early as December. The proposed deal could create the world's biggest corporate combination, but regulatory hurdles, Tesla's China operations and US national security concerns could complicate the transaction.
items.text: Elon Musk's SpaceX and Tesla Inc are progressing in merger negotiations, and the two companies could announce what would become the world's biggest-ever corporate deal as early as December, Bloomberg reported. The discussions could also extend into early 2027, depending on how negotiations progress. The boards and advisers of both companies are working out the terms of the proposed combination, including the governance structure of the merged entity, according to the report. The proposed merger would bring Musk's electric vehicle, energy storage, rocket and satellite businesses under one corporate umbrella. The rationale for the combination is reportedly centred on the companies' shared ambition to expand the use of artificial intelligence across areas such as space operations, autonomous vehicles and humanoid robots. The proposed combination could face regulatory and operational hurdles, particularly because of the companies' contrasting business interests in the US and China. One of the key issues under discussion is how Tesla's operations in China would be ring-fenced, Bloomberg reported. items.text: Nvidia, the chipmaker at the centre of the global artificial intelligence boom, faces a crucial leadership transition following the sudden resignation of co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang. With chief financial officer Colette Kress stepping in as interim CEO, investors will be watching whether the company can maintain its technological leadership and growth momentum without the man who led it for 33 years. Huang, 63, resigned on Thursday following revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China. He also relinquished his board seat. Nvidia did not provide a reason for his departure. Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years at companies including Cisco and Microsoft, will lead the company while its board searches for a successor. The board has also named Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as its chair. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. Kress joined the company in 2013. items.blurb: Ola Electric’s Revenue Dips In Q2 Ola Electric’s Q2 FY27 performance told a tale of two extremes. While revenues continued…
items.text: Ola Electric’s Q2 FY27 performance told a tale of two extremes. While revenues continued to decline and cash burn persisted, aggressive cost discipline helped narrow some of the losses. With supply chain woes worsening, did Ola Electric pay the price for its past mistakes in Q2? Supply Woes Bite: The EV maker’s Q2 performance was defined by supply chain constraints, with component and charger bottlenecks restricting vehicle output and triggering a sharp sales decline. The incident, which sparked criticism among archeologists online, underscores a growing tension in science as amateurs wielding increasingly powerful AI tools parachute into specialist fields, often without the expertise needed to understand what they are looking at. Local communities are often already well aware of sites in their area. For specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed decisions, and develop more sustainable materials without compromising performance. Girish Rao, vice president of information technology at Lubrizol, says the company is building a digital foundation that connects business processes, modern data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support its research and development (R&D) teams. Their goal is to combine decades of accumulated technical data with the deep expertise of chemists and engineers who understand customer needs as well as the physical constraints of their work. Data scientists can help identify patterns, test new hypotheses, and model possibilities before researchers conduct physical experiments. items.blurb: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially…
items.text: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy. When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill and wrote that its mandates for chip tracking were “new, untested, and potentially infeasible.”

But spending a few days in Data Center Alley left me wondering if it’s really the proxy that Lehane describes. I came away convinced that the data center backlash is more about electricity than Big Tech admits. items.text: Zupee has laid off its entire workforce and is on the verge of shutting down operations, weeks after announcing an AI pivot. The developments raise questions about whether the AI pivot was a genuine business transition or an attempt to mask the impending shutdown, and what happens to the nearly $120 Mn raised by the startup. Zupee has discontinued its gaming operations, shut down NeoAstro and Zupee Studio, while its proposed acquisition of microdrama startup Vertical TV also fell through. Delhi NCR-based gaming startup Zupee has nothing more to lose. For one, it has laid off its entire workforce. Then, its announcement of a pivot towards AI has failed to see the light of day. According to sources, the startup has provided severance pay to the affected employees, covering the period until January 2027, and its October pivot was a veiled attempt to present the impending closure. The final round of layoffs coincided with Zupee’s public announcement of its foray into AI, Inc42 has learnt. items.headline: OpenAI Brings API Inference Residency To India To Deepen Enterprise AI Adoption

items.text: ChatGPT maker OpenAI has introduced API inference residency in India, allowing eligible businesses to process supported GPT-6 Luna workloads within the country The move addresses data localisation requirements that have been a barrier to AI adoption among regulated businesses and increases competition for Indian AI companies offering locally hosted models Details: The service supports GPT-6 Luna through the Responses and Chat Completions APIs, with both processing and supported customer data storage taking place in India ChatGPT maker OpenAI has introduced local inference and data processing for its APIs in India, adding to its efforts to expand the commercialisation of ChatGPT in its largest market. For context, local data inferencing allows businesses to ensure that both API requests and the computing required to generate responses take place within India for supported workloads. It is initially available for the GPT-6 Luna model and extends OpenAI’s existing data residency options in the country.
